method: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md; atomscan slow-mode before/after; cleave facts including decoded-string views; direct archive inspection; rizin control-flow and data-flow tracing; independent PE/AuthentiCode digest calculation. No specimen executed. Reputation, labels, existing reviews and ML scores did not establish behavior.

gem.execution: On require, the module body constructs TCPSocket to 66.78.40.218:32768, reopens STDIN/STDOUT/STDERR onto that same socket, and execs /bin/sh -i. No user action, authentication or opt-in is checked inside the library. There is no gem extension/install hook; this is require-time, not installation-time execution.
gem.other_content: Packaged SVG runs alert(0x539); README embeds an SVG URL. These demonstrate a test payload, not theft or another distinct hostile outcome. No extra hostile trait was invented for the SVG.
gem.judgment: MALICIOUS: unauthenticated remote shell to an unrelated public endpoint is inconsistent with an ordinary test library. The test/do-not-use wording is weighed, but does not make the default remote shell appropriate. Authorized lab use and destination ownership are unknown.
gem.coverage_gap: Only one distinct hostile behavior is supported. Preserve the existing reverse-shell rule on the gem, data.tar.gz and Ruby member; duplicate shell objectives would not add behavior coverage.

storm.identification: Damaged StormAttack resource-DLL installer/injector; collector WannaCry name is unsupported by the code.
execution_paths: CRT entry 0x402674 calls dispatcher 0x401cb0. Mode at 0x404120 equals 3, selecting 0x401900 Active Setup setup followed by 0x401390 self-deletion. Other installation modes remain code capabilities, not observed execution.

0x401900 makes a GUID-named EXE, writes its path to HKLM Active Setup Installed Components/<GUID>/StubPath as REG_EXPAND_SZ at 0x401a4b, reads and patches its own image with CRT I/O, writes a clone with fwrite, and starts the clone at 0x401b7e.

Mode 1 calls 0x402460 to extract resource type DLL/id 101 and write it, then 0x401260 deletes LanmanServer/Parameters/ServiceDLL and writes a replacement REG_EXPAND_SZ DLL path (RegDeleteValueA at 0x401320; RegSetValueExA at 0x40133e).
0x401150 creates an unrelated target selected by 0x4010c0, allocates remote memory, writes the DLL path, resolves Kernel32.LoadLibraryA and hands it to CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d.
0x401fd0 copies itself, applies Hidden+System attributes at 0x402181 and creates/starts an automatic service. 0x401390 constructs COMSPEC /c del <short self path> > nul and launches a helper process.
storm.limitations: The entire .rsrc is zero-filled (40960 bytes), resource_count=0. Resource extraction cannot produce the configured DLL from these bytes. Code indicates design/capabilities, not successful installation, injection or working DDoS functionality. No active WannaCry ransomware behavior is established.
storm.signature: Certificate structure and signer identify Microsoft, but the attached signature does not bind this image. Independently computed image SHA256 a52cca7e337c18c6a7b0768a934ebf29cf9bef56311f318f5ae8fc1e470f5067 differs from signed digest 7623585f06acde83b65a1ac76f77f13ff62236c15259d8f3bc82b6ce9c53184a. Certificate file span is [61440,81232). Preserve both digest-mismatch findings.
storm.judgment: MALICIOUS: core-service DLL replacement, persistent self-copy, remote DLL handoff, hidden service installation and self-removal collectively distinguish this from an ordinary installer/debugger. Damage limits runtime functionality but does not supply a legitimate purpose. Deployment authorization and the missing original DLL are unknown.

gand.identification: GandCrab native ransomware payload, internal registration version 2.3.1r, with a reflective loader export and modified section names.
execution_paths: Entry 0x10004b20 enforces a derived mutex, launches a helper thread, calls application termination at 0x100048c0, initializes victim/ransom-note information at 0x100042b0 and creates key material via 0x10006550 -> 0x100063e0.

0x100048c0 builds a table of 39 database/Office/mail process names, enumerates Toolhelp entries, compares each image name, opens a matching PID with PROCESS_TERMINATE and passes that handle to TerminateProcess at 0x10004aa4. AV product names elsewhere are used for discovery; the matchers do not bind them as kill targets.

0x100063e0 calls CryptGenKey with CALG_RSA_KEYX (0xa400), exports public/private key blobs and releases the provider. 0x10005860 serializes host information and key material into a registration request, transforms/encodes it, and calls the WinINet client via 0x100054f0. It retries with Sleep until a successful reply; received key data is decoded with CryptStringToBinaryA.

0x10003ff0 enumerates usable drive roots and creates traversal workers. 0x100037b0 reads victim file contents, applies the cipher path via 0x100036d0/0x10001020, rewinds and rewrites the same file, appends encrypted key/metadata, closes and renames it. 0x10006660 imports the received key and uses CryptEncrypt to wrap file key material.

0x10006d40 constructs a ransom-note path, creates the note file and passes its plaintext bytes to WriteFile. The note is a UTF-16 buffer at RVA 0x12000 (file offset 0xfc00), XORed with 0x05 for 0xa38 bytes. 0x100042b0 decodes it in place using an all-0x05 SIMD vector and scalar tail. Decoded note demands payment for the private key and supplies TOR/TOX contact instructions.

0x100045b0 constructs wmic.exe plus shadowcopy delete for one OS branch; the other constructs cmd.exe /c vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet. Both feed ShellExecuteW at 0x100047a3. The command words are immediate stack stores, not ordinary strings.

Self-path from GetModuleFileNameW flows into 0x10003db0. That helper formats /c timeout -c 5 & del "%s" /f /q and starts cmd.exe. It is self-cleanup code; the unusual timeout flag may prevent the intended delay, not the separate DEL after ampersand.

The reflective loader walks PE structures and imports. No operator-command backdoor is established by VirtualAlloc and the cmd.exe name: those APIs and the name also occur in local copy/cleanup and buffer-allocation paths.
gand.judgment: MALICIOUS: actual file rewriting/encryption, attacker key exchange, payment note, deliberate application termination and shadow-copy deletion establish extortion and recovery inhibition. No user-facing legitimate encryption workflow or consent is present. Runtime server reachability, execution success and deployment circumstances are unknown.

rule_review.preserved: All original reverse-shell, persistence, injection, ransomware/family detections, signature findings and accurate primitives remain, with relocations recorded below. No package/dependency exceptions were used; gem has no fetched dependency supplying behavior.
rule_review.added: Two x86 stack-built shadow-removal observations and a hostile ransomware+shell+shadow-removal composite; notable CryptoAPI key generation and export; notable delayed DEL template.
rule_review.crashpad_correction: The old Crashpad identity required only section name CPADinfo. GandCrab instead places ordinary imports/configuration there, with no CrashpadInfo header. Tighten to the official signature/size/version layout at the section start. Remove the duplicate Chromium CPADinfo identity and have the three-part Chromium layout consumer require the actual CrashpadInfo header. Remove the Crashpad suppressor from a neutral remote-memory API profile so valid library identity also retains accurate capabilities. The prior positive fixture is a 716-byte import fixture with CPADinfo pointing beyond EOF; adjust its expectation to match what its bytes support.
rule_review.diagnostic_relocation: Move rsaenh initialization-failure text from ransom/encrypt/capi to micro-behaviors/crypto/provider, retaining its matcher, notable level, PE/DLL Windows scope and its ransomware consumer.
rule_review.backdoor_correction: Unsigned executable allocation plus cmd.exe text does not bind command input, shell execution, cross-process injection, or a backdoor; the rule did not even require an unsigned-signature fact. Move its three required observations to notable micro-behaviors/mem/alloc/executable::executable-allocation-cmd-name-profile and remove unsupported T1055/T1059 intent mappings. Remove its library/signer/product suppressors because these neutral capabilities are accurate in legitimate tools as well. Preserve the real reverse shell and target-bound DLL injection detections independently.
rule_review.termination_relocation: The security-process-name/enumeration/termination profiles do not bind the killed PID to a security-product name. Move both profiles and the derived HTTP profile to micro-behaviors/process/terminate/kill with accurate API-co-occurrence names. Preserve matchers, sizes, scopes, severity, exclusions, downgrades and every exact consumer. Remove the unsupported defense-impairment mapping on the profile that carried it. All original suspicious observations remain at the same effective level on the sample.
rule_review.consumer_audit: Exact consumers in GandCrab/Elex identity, injection toolkit and WinHTTP loader profiles were updated without changing thresholds or roles. C2 ancestor selectors have no affected positive consumer. The only impact/degrade parent selector is an ELF-only packet-filter rule, disjoint from the PE profiles. Broad process-termination consumers either already require a termination atom (so membership adds no new truth) or target source types disjoint from PE/DLL. Crypto directory consumers already match these inputs through existing encryption/provider primitives.
rule_review.material_losses: No supported attack behavior lost on any original or the additional Avzhan specimen, including embedded members. On GandCrab, two unsupported CPADinfo-only library identities disappear; the rsaenh diagnostic and two security/termination observations move to accurate homes. The subsequently unmasked generic allocation/cmd finding is retained as a notable capability instead of a hostile backdoor claim.
rule_review.remaining_gaps: The batch has source and transport primitives for host/key registration, but no new rule is presented as a bound host-to-HTTP or generated-private-key-to-send data-flow detection. The generic profiles cannot prove AV termination. Ruby supports only one distinct hostile result; duplicating it to satisfy a count would be inaccurate.

controls.coverage: Original GandCrab; valid Crashpad v1 headers of two structure sizes; label-only/malformed original import fixture; wrong header magic/version; each shadow command independently removed and both removed; missing encryption API; missing key-generation/export imports; benign local executable-memory/cmd co-occurrence and near misses. Correct ransomware detection survives command mutations. A valid library header does not suppress accurate remote APIs.
controls.outside_batch: The named-path specimen 83a9d1cb3a1c (Avzhan-family code) was rescanned before/after. All 188 outer findings, all 55 embedded-PE findings and all seven hostile behaviors remain unchanged. Additional repository FFplay and NSIS plugin controls retain all 52/29 findings and zero suspicious/hostile findings. Tor was inspected as a benign near miss and does not supply the allocation/cmd or HTTP/termination profiles.

controls.external: GHSA-86pf-258h-xmh8 corroborates the independently read gem source. Both provided Triage URLs were inaccessible through the web tool; neither sandbox label established the native verdicts.

classifier: All three aggregate scans remain HOSTILE. Probabilities: gem 0.9711638 unchanged; StormAttack 0.99 unchanged; GandCrab 0.97 -> 0.98. A remaining leaf-classifier miss is the gem Ruby reverse-shell member (0.003803541...) and inner tar (0.002333154...), despite an accurate hostile reverse-shell finding in both. These probabilities and archive findings are unchanged. No traits were inflated to compensate. The model also reports feature schema v18 versus extractor v19; this is a model/extractor limitation, not sample exculpation.
